title: Restorative Yoga for Fatigue (Viparita Karani)
content: Viparita Karani, or Legs-Up-The-Wall pose, is a restorative yoga practice that is excellent for combating exhaustion and fatigue. Lie on your back with your sitting bones close to a wall and extend your legs straight up the wall. This pose helps drain lymphatic fluid from the legs, improves circulation, and calms the nervous system. Combine it with gentle Pranayama (deep breathing) for maximum benefit. It is ideal for those who feel burnt out or physically tired.

title: Ayurvedic Diet for Fatigue and Low Energy
content: An Ayurvedic fatigue diet focuses on balancing Vata dosha, which is often responsible for feeling exhausted or depleted. Include warm, nourishing foods like kitchari (rice and mung dal), warm milk with a pinch of nutmeg before bed, and sweet, juicy fruits like peaches and melons. Avoid dry, cold, or highly processed foods. Incorporate grounding spices such as ginger, cardamom, and cinnamon. Staying well-hydrated with warm water or herbal teas also helps restore energy levels.

title: Surya Namaskar Steps and Benefits (Sun Salutation)
content: Surya Namaskar, or Sun Salutation, is a sequence of 12 powerful yoga asanas. It is best performed early morning on an empty stomach. Ek complete round consists of two sets, starting with the right leg and then the left. Regular practice provides a great cardiovascular workout and improves blood circulation. It helps with weight loss (वजन घटाना) and strengthens muscles and joints. Its known to improve digestion and reduce stress (*tanav*). People with high blood pressure, hernia, or back problems should consult a doctor or certified instructor before performing it. Each posture is coordinated with your breath, which makes it a very calming practice.

title: Anulom Vilom Pranayama ke Fayde (Alternate Nostril Breathing)
content: Anulom Vilom is a powerful pranayama to calm the mind and relieve stress. Sit in a comfortable meditative pose with your spine straight. Use your right thumb to close your right nostril and inhale slowly through the left. Then, close your left nostril with your ring finger, release your thumb, and exhale through the right nostril. Now inhale through the right and exhale through the left. This is one round. Start with 5-10 rounds. It helps balance the Tridoshas (Vata, Pitta, Kapha) in the body. Contraindications: Do not practice if you have a cold, cough, or fever. Best time is subah (morning) before breakfast. It improves patience and concentration.

title: Balanced Indian Diet Chart for Healthy Lifestyle
content: A balanced diet is key to good health. Your plate should be a mix of carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals. For breakfast, opt for poha, upma, or idli instead of fried foods. Lunch can be 2 rotis, a bowl of dal, sabzi, and a portion of salad. Dinner should be the lightest meal; khichdi or dal with a vegetable stir-fry is a good option. Include seasonal fruits and vegetables. Make sure to drink at least 8-10 glasses of paani (water) daily. Avoid processed sugar and excessive salt. For non-vegetarians, grilled chicken or fish are healthier than fried preparations. Snacking on nuts and seeds is a great way to manage cravings.

title: Kapalbhati for Beginners: Step-by-Step Guide
content: Kapalbhati, or Skull Shining Breath, is an invigorating pranayama that cleanses the body. It involves active, forceful exhalation and passive inhalation. Sit comfortably with a straight spine. Take a deep breath in, and then start exhaling in short, powerful bursts. Your stomach should pump inwards with each exhalation. Start with a round of 20-30 pumps. You can do up to 3 rounds with breaks in between. This practice is excellent for stimulating the digestive system and improving metabolic rate, aiding in weight loss. Contraindications: Avoid if you are pregnant, have high blood pressure, heart disease, hernia, or epilepsy. Perform on an empty stomach, preferably in the morning.

title: Vrikshasana (Tree Pose) for Better Balance and Focus
content: Vrikshasana, or Tree Pose, is a fundamental balancing asana in yoga. It improves focus, concentration, and physical balance. Stand straight and find a fixed point to gaze at. Shift your weight to your left foot and place your right foot on your inner left thigh, avoiding the knee joint. Press your palms together in a prayer position at your chest. Hold for 30 seconds to a minute, breathing deeply. This pose strengthens the legs, ankles, and spine. It helps relieve sciatica and can reduce flat feet. Those with high blood pressure should avoid raising their arms overhead. Be patient; balance comes with practice. It helps calm the mind and reduces *chinta* (anxiety).

title: Meet Our Head Instructor: Yogi Devvrat
content: Yogi Devvrat is a certified RYT 500 Yoga Alliance instructor with over 15 years of experience. He began his journey in Rishikesh, learning from traditional yoga gurus. His teaching style blends classical Hatha yoga with modern Vinyasa flow, focusing on alignment and breath. Yogi Devvrat believes that yoga is not just about asanas, but a way of life. His sessions often include pranayama and meditation to provide a holistic experience. He specializes in therapeutic yoga, helping clients manage chronic pain and stress-related ailments. Yoga ek yatra hai, manzil nahi (Yoga is a journey, not a destination), he often says. Join his Sunrise Flow class every weekday at 6:30 AM.

title: Foods to Boost Immunity (Rog Pratirodhak Chhamata)
content: A strong immune system is essential for fighting off infections. Incorporate these foods into your diet. Citrus fruits like amla, oranges, and lemons are rich in Vitamin C, a key immunity booster. Turmeric (haldi) contains curcumin, a powerful anti-inflammatory compound; add it to milk or curries. Ginger and garlic have been used for centuries for their medicinal properties. Yogurt is a great source of probiotics, which are good for gut health, where a large part of the immune system resides. Green leafy vegetables like spinach (palak) are packed with antioxidants. Almonds are a great source of Vitamin E. Its important to have a balanced diet rather than focusing on just one food.

title: Trikonasana (Triangle Pose): Technique and Benefits
content: Trikonasana, or Triangle Pose, is a foundational standing pose that stretches the entire body. Stand with your feet wide apart. Turn your right foot out 90 degrees and your left foot in slightly. Inhale, and as you exhale, extend your torso to the right, bending from the hips and placing your right hand on your shin, ankle, or the floor. Extend your left arm up to the sky. This pose stretches the hamstrings, hips, and spine, while strengthening the legs and core. It is therapeutic for stress and improves digestion by stimulating the abdominal organs. Contraindication: Avoid if you have a headache, low blood pressure, or a neck injury. Dont lock your knees. Hold for 30-60 seconds.

title: Bhramari Pranayama (Bee Breath) for Instant Calm
content: Bhramari, or Bee Breath, is an excellent technique to instantly calm an agitated mind and relieve anxiety. Sit in a comfortable position and gently close your eyes. Place your index fingers on your ears cartilage. Inhale deeply, and as you exhale, make a low-pitched humming sound like a bee, keeping your mouth closed. Continue for 5-10 rounds. The vibration of the humming sound has a soothing effect on the brain and nervous system. It is very effective in reducing high blood pressure and mitigating migraines. There are no major contraindications, but it should be done on an empty stomach. Practice it anytime you feel stressed or before sleeping for better sleep quality (*acchi neend*).

title: Hydration is Key: Paani Peene Ke Fayde
content: Staying hydrated is crucial for overall health. Water regulates body temperature, lubricates joints, and helps deliver nutrients to cells. Dehydration can cause headaches, fatigue, and poor concentration. Aim for 8-10 glasses of water per day, more if you exercise or its a hot day. Drinking water before meals can also aid in weight management by making you feel full. Its essential for kidney function and flushing out toxins. For better taste and added benefits, you can infuse your water with lemon, cucumber, or mint leaves. Dont wait until youre thirsty; sip water throughout the day. Its the simplest way to boost your physical and mental performance.

title: Shavasana (Corpse Pose) for Deep Relaxation
content: Shavasana, or Corpse Pose, is often practiced at the end of a yoga session, but it is one of the most important and difficult asanas. It allows the body to rest and absorb the benefits of the practice. Lie flat on your back, with your feet spread comfortably apart and arms resting alongside your body, palms facing up. Close your eyes and let go of your breath control. Bring your awareness to each part of your body, consciously releasing any tension (*thakaan*). This pose helps reduce blood pressure, calms the nervous system, and combats insomnia. Spend at least 5-10 minutes in Shavasana. It might seem like just lying down, but the goal is to remain aware and relaxed without falling asleep.

title: Balasana (Childs Pose): A Restorative Asana
content: Balasana, or Childs Pose, is a gentle and restorative yoga pose that can be practiced by anyone. Its a great way to take a break during a strenuous yoga session or to stretch the body after a long day of sitting. Kneel on the floor, sit back on your heels, and then fold forward, resting your forehead on the floor. Your arms can be stretched out in front of you or resting alongside your body. This pose gently stretches the hips, thighs, and ankles while relieving back and neck pain. It calms the brain and helps alleviate stress and fatigue. Hold the pose for anywhere from 30 seconds to a few minutes, focusing on deep, diaphragmatic breathing. Its a surrender pose, encouraging you to let go.

title: The Truth About Millets: Jowar, Bajra, Ragi
content: Millets are ancient grains making a comeback for their incredible health benefits. They are gluten-free and rich in fiber, protein, and antioxidants. Ragi (Finger Millet) is an excellent source of calcium, great for bone health. Jowar (Sorghum) is packed with iron and protein. Bajra (Pearl Millet) is rich in magnesium, which is good for heart health. Being high in fiber, millets keep you full for longer, aiding in weight management. They also have a low glycemic index, making them suitable for diabetics. You can easily incorporate them into your diet by swapping rice with millet or making rotis from their flour. They are not just gaon ka khana (village food) but a modern superfood for a healthy lifestyle.

title: Sheetali Pranayama (Cooling Breath) for Summer
content: Sheetali Pranayama is a breathing technique that has a cooling effect on the body and mind. It is perfect for practicing during hot weather or when feeling agitated. Sit comfortably. Roll your tongue into a tube shape and stick it out of your mouth. Inhale slowly and deeply through the tube, as if sipping air through a straw. Then, retract your tongue, close your mouth, and exhale slowly through your nostrils. Repeat 5-10 times. This pranayama cools the body, reduces mental and emotional excitation, and can help control hunger and thirst. Contraindications: Not recommended for people with low blood pressure or respiratory issues like asthma. Practice in a clean environment.
